title: Control Plane Decision Heuristics and Incident Simulation Notes
content:
Purpose and tone:
This is an operational-architecture hybrid note: decision heuristics for the control plane (what to route, when to failover, how to degrade), plus short, runnable incident simulations and embedded runbook fragments. Treat as a living doc. It is intentionally informal — contains commands, TODOs, and quick checks that on-call can run under noise.

Background summary (1-paragraph):
The control plane makes routing decisions across regions and model variants. Inputs: per-route latency P50/P95/P99, request error rates, node-level health (kube/VM), capacity signals (GPU util, queue depth), cost toggles (reserved vs burst), and manual overrides. The heuristics below are tuned for production SLOs where API 95 latency target is 200–250ms and availability target is 99.9% per region.

Quick decision heuristics (compact):
- If control-plane RPC error rate > 1% sustained for 2 minutes => mark control-plane cluster unhealthy, enable local routeless fallback (ping local agent) and notify SRE.
- If region-level egress error (5xx fraction) > 3% for 1 minute AND cross-region capacity within 15% headroom => prepare cross-region reroute (graceful weight shift, 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 mins).
- If p95 latency for a model-family > 250ms (and p50 > 120ms) for 2 sample windows of 30s => prefer lower-latency compatible model-variant and enable prefix-KV cache hotpaths.
- If persistent route flapping (same route remapped >3 times in 10m) => enable sticky routing to previous stable mapping for 30m and escalate to platform oncall.
- If autoscaler oscillation detected (scale up then down >2 cycles in 10m) => pause autoscaler, set manual capacity to last stable size, alert infra team.

Operational simulation scenarios (short, reproducible):
1) "Island" region failure (simulated network partition)
   - Goal: verify graceful cross-region failover with cached KV and minimal request duplication.
   - Pre-sim checks: ensure at least two healthy cross-region endpoints, confirm KV cache TTLs >= 60s for top 10 prefixes.
   - Run commands (on a test cluster or a canary namespace):
     - kubectl -n controlplane get pods -l app=controlplane -o wide
     - curl -sS http://controlplane-canary.svc.cluster.local/healthz | jq .
     - # simulate partition: iptables -A OUTPUT -d <region-ip> -j DROP (OR use network fault injection tool)
   - Expected behavior: local agent switches to "regional-serve" decisions with degraded bandwidth; control plane emits event route.failover.start; traffic weight migration begins 10%/min until 100% if errors persist.
   - Mitigation steps if automation fails:
     - Manually set route weights: curl -X POST https://controlplane-api/_routes/adjust -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","weights":{"us-west":0,"us-east":1}}' (use API key vault)
     - Reconcile KV caches: curl http://cache-admin.svc/evict?prefix=top-prefixes && sleep 5 && curl http://cache-admin.svc/warm?prefix=top-prefixes
   - Postmortem checks: verify no duplicate request ids in logs, ensure per-route token accounting consistent, record time to full reroute.

2) Asymmetric latency spike (regional network degradation causing high egress p95 only to a subset of backend pools)
   - Symptom: p95 spikes but p50 stable; error rates low.
   - Heuristic action: prefer model-variant with smaller context window for affected routes; increase batching window for background tasks only.
   - Quick investigation commands:
     - envoy admin: curl -s http://local-envoy/admin/clusters | grep -A3 upstream_cluster
     - check metrics: grafana link: /d/survey/controlplane?orgId=1&var-cluster=us-west (archive for run)
   - Runbook snippet:
     - 1) Pause model-variant rollout (if a rollout was ongoing).
     - 2) Set per-route override to model-variant-lite for routes with p95 > 250ms: PATCH /routes/:id {"model_override":"m-lite-v2"}
     - 3) Re-evaluate in 2 min; if p95 drops to target, schedule a change in Optimize suggestions.

3) Cache inconsistency across regions (KV mismatch causing unseen hallucination/regression)
   - Symptom: top-k token deltas in responses between regions; users report small but reproducible divergence.
   - Investigation commands:
     - redis-cli -h redis-primary INFO replication
     - curl -s http://controlplane-api/_cache/consistency?prefix=abc123 | jq .
   - Recovery runbook:
     - Replace read replicas: scale down to 0 then back up in controlled window, flush only affected prefixes using safe-evict script, warm caches from canonical snapshot.
   - Safety note: Flush should be staged: evict subset -> verify -> evict next subset. Do not global FLUSHALL in prod.

Embedded runbook fragments (copy/pasteable):
- Verify control plane health:
  - kubectl -n controlplane get pod -l role=api -o wide
  - curl -sS http://controlplane.svc.cluster.local/healthz | jq .status
  - curl -sS http://controlplane-metrics.svc:9090/api/v1/query?query=rate(controlplane_rpc_errors[1m])

- Manual regional failover (emergency):
  - Preconditions: have manual route API key, understand downstream billing delta.
  - Steps:
    1) Lock rollouts: POST /control/rollouts/lock
    2) Set route weight: POST /routes/weights {"route":"*","weights":{"regionA":0.0,"regionB":1.0}}
    3) Watch request logs for repeat errors: kubectl -n ingress logs -l app=ingress --tail=200
    4) If errors persist, fail open (route to degraded model variant) by toggling feature-flag: POST /flags/enable {"flag":"degraded-serve"}

- Reconcile accounting after failover:
  - Run ledger re-aggregation job: POST /jobs/reaggregate-usage?window=failover-interval
  - Verify per-customer quotas: curl /billing/check?customer_id=1234

Escalation matrix (light):
- Level 1 (oncall platform): triage, run diagnostics above, attempt automated mitigations in 15m window.
- Level 2 (infra + serving-runtime): invoked if automation fails or data-plane errors > 3% for >10m.
- Level 3 (engineering leads + legal/customer success): invoked on SEV-1 or if customer SLA is at risk.

Post-incident validation checklist (short):
- Confirm p95 and error rate are back within SLO for at least 30m.
- Run smoke prompts against each region (sample set of 20 prompts) and diff top-3 tokens.
- Confirm cost delta calculated and billing pipeline reconciled.
- Open follow-up action items with owners and due dates.

Decision heuristics: rationale and thresholds (why these numbers):
- 1% control-plane RPC errors: small but indicative of RPC library regression or network flakiness; we use short windows to avoid over-reacting to transient blips.
- 3% region egress errors: empirically correlated with increased user-facing 5xx within 5–15 minutes in prior incidents.
- p95 250ms: our UX studies show conversational turn feels degraded above this point.

Observability queries to keep handy (copy/paste):
- Control plane error rate: curl -s 'http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(controlplane_rpc_errors[1m])) by (region)'
- Traffic split sanity: curl -s 'http://controlplane-api/routes' | jq '.[] | {route:.id,weights:.weights}'
- Hot prefix list: curl -s 'http://telemetry-api/hot-prefixes?window=5m' | jq .

Common gotchas and notes to self:
- Don’t evict caches right before a big rollout. We’ve seen 30–40% CPU spikes when a warm cache is lost concurrently with traffic ramp.
- Autoscaler pause must be done in controlplane first, then platform autoscaler. Reversing order can cause orphan tokens.
- When testing partition simulations, use canary namespaces and ensure no customer traffic is affected — set qps-limiter to 0.1 of production.

Incidents we should simulate next (TODOs):
- Kafka backlog causing delayed routing updates (PLAT-1012 simulated heavy churn).
- Token accounting drift when we have mixed-precision quantized model variants.
- Edge-proxy TLS renewal failing in a region, causing short-lived 525s chain.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we make the 10%/min migration speed configurable per-customer? (tradeoff: safety vs speed)
- Can we add an automated checksum verification for KV warm snapshots before failover? (low-effort: compare top-n prefixes hash)
- SRE to propose a chaos experiment to force persistent cache-evictions and measure end-to-end latency delta (owner: Leila).

Appendix: short scripts and snippets (for oncall):
- Evict prefixes safely:
  - for p in $(curl -s http://telemetry-api/top-prefixes | jq -r .[]); do curl -s "http://cache-admin/evict?prefix=$p" && sleep 2; done
- Quick model-variant rollback check:
  - curl -s http://controlplane-api/routes | jq '.[] | select(.route=="/v1/generate")'

Final note: this doc is intentionally practical and contains commands that touch production. If you are not the oncall with required keys, stop and ping the oncall. Record any manual steps taken in the incident ticket.

-- Ava
